$comment: One sample of every event the server pushes down a visitor's live stream.
Both sides of the wire assert against this file and neither one owns it.
tools/check-visitor-events.ts drives the real server code and checks what it
publishes has these shapes; the Dart SDK's fake server replays these samples
rather than literals somebody typed. A key renamed on either side now breaks
It exists because of a bug it would have caught on day one: the Dart client
read 'type' and 'message' while the server sent 'kind' and 'payload', so
every agent reply was dropped before it reached the UI — and the SDK's own
test passed throughout, because its fake server had been written from the
client's expectation instead of the server's contract. Two halves agreeing
with each other and neither with production is the failure this prevents.
Values are illustrative. Only the shape is the contract: which keys exist,
and what kind of thing each holds.
$comment_message: One agent reply, carrying everything a message can carry: the note it
answers, a voice recording, and the emoji on it. Deliberately the rich case
rather than a bare sentence — the keys that go missing are the optional ones,
and a fixture showing only the simple shape is a fixture that never notices.
`quote` flattens the message being answered onto the reply instead of naming
it by id: the original may be older than the window a client holds, and a
quote that renders blank because it scrolled out of memory is worse than no
On an attachment, `kind` is what separates a recording from an audio file
somebody attached — both are audio/… and only one is drawn as a waveform.
The bars and the duration were measured by the recorder while the note was
being made, so no reader has to decode the file to draw a shape that would
be the same for all of them.
`reactions` is always present, empty on a message nobody has reacted to. A
key that appears only once somebody taps is a key every reader has to defend
against, on the commonest message there is.

payload.body: Yes — it's the one with the blue door

quote.preview: Is it the house on the corner?

$comment_reaction: An emoji landed on a message, from either side.
Carries the whole message, not the one emoji: reactions are a set with one
slot per person, so a client applying a delta has to know what was already
there to know whether this one replaces it — which is exactly what the two
sides disagree about during two taps in quick succession. Replacing the row
`by` is written from the reader's point of view: 'visitor' is the person
holding the phone, whichever side of the desk put it there.
